newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM to cut copper production costs.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM to cut copper production costs.

text.p: Poland's KGHM copper concern, to start trade on Warsaw and London bourses on July 10, aims to cut production costs to $1,465 per tonne in 2000 from $1,952 in 1996, KGHM's president said on Friday.
Stanislaw Siewierski told a news conference the company expected to bring down costs of producing one pound of copper to $0.79 this year from $0.88 in 1996.
"Our main goal is to increase KGHM's value and one of the main tools for that is to cut production costs to $0.65 per pound of copper in 2000 from $0.88 in 1996," Siewierski said.
"We would like to cut production costs to $0.75 per pound in 1998 and to $0.69 in 1999," he added.

He said KGHM, the fifth largest copper producer and the largest silver producer in the world, also wanted to raise copper production to 433,000 tonnes this year and to 470,000 in 2001, from 424,700 in 1996.
It plans to increase its silver production to about 1,000 tonnes this year from 933 tonnes last year.
"The one million kilograms of silver level is roughly the ceiling for our current silver processing capabilities," Siewierski said.
